passages.original: quæ non alias semper indicta est, nisi cum aliquid in pravis sensibus novum, aut in assertione dogmatum emersit ambiguum : ut in commune tractantibus. si quae esset obscurilas, sacerdotalis deliberationis illuminaret auctoritas ; sicut primum Arii, ac deinde Nestorii, postremum Dioscori atque Eutychetis fieri coegit impietas. Et (quod misericordia Christi Dei nostri salvatoris avertat !) intimandum est abominabile esse contra sententias totius orbis Domini sacerdotum et principum utriusque rectorum, damnatos reos restituere, reduci exsules, relegatos in causa nefariæ conjurationis absolvi.
passages.english: [a synod] which has never been convened except when something new has arisen among perverse opinions, or something doubtful in the statement of doctrines, so that, as they discussed it in common, if there were any obscurity, the authority of priestly deliberation might illuminate it; just as the impiety first of Arius, and then of Nestorius, and lastly of Dioscorus and Eutyches compelled to be done. And (may the mercy of Christ our God and Saviour avert it!) it must be made known that it is abominable, against the judgements of the Lord's priests of the whole world and of the princes who rule both [parts], to restore condemned culprits, to bring back exiles, and to acquit those banished in the case of a wicked conspiracy.
passages.notes: 'quæ' refers back to the synod (synodi) in the preceding context. 'obscurilas' is read as 'obscuritas'. 'principum utriusque rectorum' is understood as the rulers of both parts of the empire, East and West; the syntax is awkward and may be corrupt. The parenthetical prayer 'quod... avertat' sits oddly before 'intimandum est'. It probably refers to the prospect of restoring the condemned.
